title: Olfactory combinatorial 3-of-24 constant-weight wordline decoder
idea: About 400 olfactory receptor types encode trillions of odors combinatorially. Replace one-hot predecode with a constant-weight code: each local wordline driver connects to a unique triplet of 24 shared select lines (2,024 triplets) through a vertical 3-gate stacked transistor. Only the triplet with all three lines high fires, and every other triplet has at most two high.
why: Fact 7: about 2-3x fewer predecode lines and decoder transistors than tree decoders, so row-decode area falls ~30%.

title: Ant-colony refresh: per-mat thermal sensors with neighbor gossip
idea: Ant colonies act on local quorum, not central command. Each mat gets a tiny ring-oscillator thermometer; mats share readings with neighbors over a 1-bit chain and each sets its own refresh interval, so cool mats far from hot spots refresh less.
why: On-die gradients of 5-15 C mean most mats over-refresh; local scheduling cuts refresh operations ~30-50% (fact 3).

title: Software-switchable twin-cell mode per subarray
idea: Add a switch in each SA stripe so a subarray runs either as 1T1C (full capacity) or as 2T2C differential pairs (half capacity, ~4-8x retention and margin); the OS chooses the mode per subarray by workload and temperature.
why: Refresh and reliability (facts 3, 9): a flexible density-versus-retention trade lets marginal old-line dies ship and lets hot deployments skip most refresh.

title: Apartment-tower shared lobby: one sense die serves eight array dies
idea: An apartment tower shares one lobby and elevator bank. Stack eight array-only dies whose short bitline segments drop through hybrid-bonded vertical vias into one shared sense/decode die, with a tier-select switch at each die's bitline foot so one die connects at a time.
why: Water/periphery: periphery wafers per bit fall ~8x and array dies need no CMOS module, so periphery-attributable water falls ~10x with no new chemistry; added via capacitance is the physics risk.

title: Switched-capacitor bitline doubler magnifies signal before latching
idea: After charge sharing, switches reconnect the two halves of each bitline pair in series (a switched-capacitor voltage doubler), MAGNIFYING the differential signal ~1.8x before the latch fires, which lets VARY MINIFY to ~0.5-0.6 V.
why: Fact 10: CV2 array energy -65%; alternatively relaxes Cs ~40% (Fact 1).

title: Display-fab glass panels manufacture DRAM periphery at Gen-8.5 scale
idea: Box: Si array die x Si access x LTPS/IGZO sense amps x panel-level bonding x glass substrate x display fab. Sense amps, decoders and pumps are made as high-variability LTPS/oxide TFT circuits on large glass panels in under-used display fabs and bonded to array-only dies; the 1% budget absorbs TFT Vt scatter.
why: Capital intensity: display area costs ~1/50 of 300 mm logic per m^2; frees DRAM-fab capacity and adds a new supply base.

title: SiN photonic H-tree replaces the die's global data wires
idea: PECVD silicon-nitride waveguides (<=350 C), electro-optic polymer ring modulators (cured <=200 C) and sputtered polycrystalline Ge detectors form an optical global bus from banks to I/O, MAGNIFYING bandwidth per wire ~20x.
why: Fact 5: on-die global data-movement energy from ~1 pJ/bit to ~0.2 pJ/bit with far fewer global wires; low-temperature poly-Ge responsivity is the risk.

title: Po: bitlines amplify themselves — oxide TFT segment preamps
idea: Po: a bitline with gain built into it. Cut each bitline into 32-cell local segments, each sensed by a BEOL IGZO thin-film gain transistor stacked above the capacitor array whose gate is the segment node; the tiny segment capacitance (~1/8 of a full bitline) gives ~6x larger swing that the TFT converts into current on a global bitline.
why: Capacitor wall (#1) and 3D (#2): Cs can drop from ~5 fF to ~1 fF at equal signal, enabling shallow capacitors that suit stacked tiers.

title: CCD charge-transfer bitline segments feeding a tiny sense node
idea: Astronomical CCDs move charge packets with 99.9999% efficiency instead of sharing them; each bitline is split into 8-16 clocked transfer gates that shift the cell's packet to a ~0.3 fF floating diffusion at the SA rather than dumping it onto a 50-100 fF bitline. The SA sees roughly 10x the voltage of conventional charge sharing.
why: Breaks the Cs/Cbl ratio rule behind fact 1: ~10x signal allows ~1 fF cells or 4x longer bitlines; the transfer adds ~3-8 ns.

title: Rank-order sensing of constant-weight codes needs no threshold
idea: Time jump: let charge decay for minutes, because only ordering matters; data is stored in 8-cell groups as a 4-of-8 constant-weight code (70 words, ~6 bits) and a winner-take-all sense circuit picks the four highest-charge cells. Decay shifts absolute levels but not the order until the weakest '1' meets the strongest '0', so optimizer state rewritten each training step never needs refresh.
why: Threshold-free sensing stretches usable retention ~10-100x (fact 3) for 24% capacity overhead, enough to delete refresh for data rewritten within its window.

title: Gallium-oxide access-transistor arrays bonded onto silicon periphery
idea: Material jump with a time jump to years of retention: 4.8 eV-gap beta-Ga2O3 transistors, grown on native substrates and layer-transferred, form the cell array with off-currents below 10^-21 A, and the slower array is read through time-domain integrating sense amps on a bonded Si CMOS wafer; no refresh circuitry is built.
why: Retention beyond product life means zero refresh (fact 3) while fast Si periphery is kept; a crystalline wide-gap route distinct from IGZO.

title: FD-SOI back-biased hold mode for idle mats
idea: Time jump between ns access mode and minute-scale hold mode: access transistors sit on fully depleted SOI, so there is no storage-junction leakage to substrate, and the periphery switches an idle mat's buried back plane to -2 V (a held voltage, no current), suppressing subthreshold leakage ~10^3-10^4 so data idle for minutes survives with no refresh.
why: Removes junction and subthreshold leakage paths (fact 3) -> zero refresh for data idle under minutes; static back bias draws no refresh power.

title: Po: let the sense amp guess — early fire plus ECC
idea: Po: a sense amp allowed to be wrong. Fire the latch at ~40% of the normal signal-development time and accept raw bit errors ~1e-5, then correct with a strong on-die BCH code over 512-bit words computed in the periphery during the column access.
why: Capacitor wall (#1): either tRCD falls ~30% or Cs can drop from ~5 fF to ~3 fF at today's timing, avoiding AR-115 pillars; the ECC logic costs ~3% die, far less than a capacitor-etch generation.

title: One-mask NEMS relays for leakage-free row decoders
idea: Revive the relay computer (Zuse's Z3) at nanoscale. Lateral electrostatic relays are patterned in an existing upper metal layer and released by a single added air-gap etch mask, giving zero-leakage, abrupt-switching pass gates for row decoders and bank power switches.
why: Zero off-state leakage in decoders and power gates cuts standby power, and moving decoding into BEOL shrinks the silicon periphery (fact 7).

title: Eliminate plasma fin etch: crystallographic TMAH wet-etched sense-amp transistors
idea: On the bonded periphery wafer, use (110) silicon, where TMAH etches vertical {111} sidewalls at ~100:1 anisotropy, to form SA fins through an Al2O3 hard mask patterned with BCl3. The fins come out with atomically smooth walls and no fluorinated or HBr plasma.
why: Smooth walls cut Vt mismatch ~20-30%, so SA devices can shrink at the same offset; the fin plasma-etch module disappears.

title: Asymmetry: leak-aware reference skew plus non-leaking-state data encoding
idea: TRIZ #4 Asymmetry: cells leak only from '1' toward '0', so the sense reference is shifted toward the '0' side, letting decaying '1's stay readable much longer, while the controller applies a per-64 B invert flag so that at least half the stored bits sit in the non-leaking discharged state that tolerates the reduced margin.
why: Fact 3: refresh interval can roughly double (refresh energy and bandwidth ~-40-50%) and fewer bits are exposed to the retention tail; costs one flag bit per 64 B and a trimmed reference.

title: Oxide-TFT predecoders and test logic built over the array
idea: Move slow, low-drive periphery (row predecoders, fuse latches, test-mode logic, mode registers) into BEOL IGZO thin-film transistor layers built over the cell array, leaving only the sense amps and fast IO in silicon.
why: Periphery 49% (fact 7): moving ~15-20% of die area into the space over the array gives ~1.2x bits per wafer without wafer bonding.

title: Cold forging: 77 K-operated 180 nm DRAM with planar capacitors
idea: Like cold forging, which gains strength by working metal cold, run a 180 nm planar-capacitor DRAM in liquid nitrogen. Junction and subthreshold leakage fall by >10^6 and SA transistors gain ~2x transconductance with lower noise, so small ~2-3 fF planar caps sense reliably and refresh nearly disappears.
why: No tall capacitors, EUV or refresh for a datacenter memory tier on cheap U.S. 180 nm wafers; this offsets part of the ~10x density penalty and cooling cost, and SA area shrinks from better gm and matching.

title: Ferroelectric polarization kick boosts wordlines without charge pumps
idea: Ideal result: a 3 V wordline from a 1 V supply with no pump. A ferroelectric capacitor at each wordline driver output releases its remanent charge (~20-40 uC/cm^2) on polarization switching, bootstrapping the wordline above the supply locally.
why: Voltage floor and periphery (facts 7, 10): removes VPP charge pumps (several % die area and ~30% pump efficiency loss).

title: Hydraulic-accumulator antiferroelectric reservoirs replace oversized wordline charge pumps
idea: Like a hydraulic accumulator that banks pressure for peak demand, put antiferroelectric ZrO2 capacitors under the sub-wordline driver strips. A small pump charges them slowly, and during activate bursts they release a large charge at a near-constant voltage plateau set by the field-induced phase switch-back.
why: VPP pumps are sized for tFAW peak bursts; AFE energy density is ~5-10x MOS caps and its plateau self-regulates, shrinking pump + decap area ~50-70% (several % of die) and cutting pump losses.

title: Voltage-to-time sensing with one TDC shared by 32 bitlines
idea: Convert the signal domain: each bitline drives a current-starved inverter whose delay encodes the ~100 mV signal; edges from 32 bitlines are serialized into one shared time-to-digital converter that also outputs a margin value.
why: Fact 7: per-bitline hardware shrinks to ~2 transistors; the margin output feeds retention-aware refresh (fact 3).

title: DUV-only arrays with loose CD control, weak-cell tail coded away
idea: Box: pillar cap x Si access x soft-decision SA x standard integration x bulk Si x ArF-immersion SAQP without EUV. Critical layers are patterned with DUV multipatterning at wider CD variation, letting ~1% of cells be too weak or leaky; soft sensing plus the code covers them.
why: EUV layers drop from 5-7 to 0, cutting capex and single-supplier dependency; wafer cost ~-20%.

title: Spinning-jenny sensing: one amplifier spins across sixteen gain-cell bitlines
idea: As one spinning-jenny wheel drove many spindles, pair non-destructive-read gain cells with one shared, high-quality sense amp per 16 read bitlines through a 1:16 mux. Reads do not destroy data, so only requested columns are sensed and no row restore is needed.
why: SA count drops 16x (SA area from ~15-20% of die to ~2%) and the 128x page overfetch disappears (~5.9 pJ per useful bit toward <1 pJ).

title: One shared SerDes chiplet replaces eight dies' wide PHYs
idea: MINIFY each DRAM die's PHY, DLL and I/O ring (~8-10% of area) to a narrow on-package bridge port, and MAGNIFY a single 224G SerDes chiplet that serializes traffic for eight dies.
why: Fact 7: ~8% of die area returned to cells and fewer pins per bit; like a CXL buffer but pulled inside the package.

title: Per-stripe adaptive array voltage regulated by sensed margin
idea: Put a micro-LDO in every SA stripe and close the loop with a replica sense pair on a programmable reference: the regulator lowers that subarray's VARY until measured margin reaches target, so strong subarrays run near 0.7 V while weak ones stay at 1.0 V.
why: Voltage floor (fact 10): ~20% average VARY drop gives ~35% lower array CV^2 energy, with per-region guardbands instead of one worst-case guardband per die.

title: Self-timed sense completion replaces worst-case DRAM timing margins
idea: Substitute fixed worst-case timing (tRCD/tRAS guard bands) with asynchronous completion detection. Each sense latch drives dual-rail outputs, and a C-element tree over a mat raises 'row sensed' as soon as the slowest latch has actually resolved, so column access starts at the real finish time.
why: Latency and bandwidth: typical rows resolve 25-35% faster than the worst corner, recovering tRCD time and part of the 10-20% bandwidth lost to refresh (fact 3).

title: Roll-to-roll high-k decoupling film laminated onto the die
idea: Worse: fill periphery with MOS decoupling capacitors to keep supply noise down. Flip: laminate a roll-to-roll-coated thin-film decoupling sheet, such as a BaTiO3-polymer nanocomposite between foil electrodes, onto the die top or package through a printed bump array.
why: Periphery area (fact 7): on-die decap is several percent of die; moving it to a laminate frees area and adds lower-inductance bulk capacitance.

title: Refresh interval set by 1% failure point, scrubbed by ECC
idea: Box: standard cap x Si access x SA plus decode-on-refresh x controller scrub x bulk Si x standard. Retention is specified where 1% of cells fail instead of at the 1e-9 tail, which stretches refresh ~16-30x; each refresh pass reads through the decoder and writes back corrected data so errors never pile up.
why: Refresh energy (16-33% of idle) and bandwidth loss (10-20%) cut >90%; the ~13 fA leakage tail stops mattering.

title: Negative-capacitance bitline dielectric makes the bitline vanish electrically
idea: Ideal result: a bitline with zero capacitance, so every femtofarad of cell charge becomes signal. Closest achievable: line the bitline-to-plate spacer with a thin stabilized HZO negative-capacitance layer in series with the parasitic, so effective Cbl drops 2-3x while staying hysteresis-free in the small-signal range.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): transfer ratio Cs/(Cs+Cbl) rises from ~0.1 to ~0.25, allowing ~2x smaller Cs or 2x longer bitlines (half the SA stripes, fact 7).

title: SiGe HBT preamplifier stage with sub-millivolt offset matching
idea: Nuclear instruments and 200 C downhole electronics prefer bipolars for matching and hardness; insert a SiGe HBT differential pre-amp (behind a MOS source follower so base current never drains the bitline) ahead of the CMOS latch. HBT Vbe mismatch is ~0.3-1 mV versus ~10-15 mV for minimum MOS pairs.
why: Required bitline signal drops from ~100 mV to ~25 mV: Cs can fall ~3x or bitlines grow ~3x longer, attacking facts 1 and 7.

title: Oscillator timed by real DRAM cells clocks refresh
idea: Build a relaxation oscillator whose timing element is a group of real array cells (same capacitor and access transistor) discharging to a threshold; its period tracks actual retention across temperature, voltage and process and directly sets each bank's refresh interval.
why: Refresh (fact 3): replaces the worst-case 64 ms plus temperature bins with tracked retention, typically 2-4x fewer refreshes for most dies and conditions.

title: Radio aperture synthesis: twin mini-cells summed on one bitline
idea: Like an interferometer combining small dishes into one big aperture, store each bit in two half-size capacitors on different tiers/wordlines that fire together onto one bitline; their charges add, so each capacitor needs only ~2.5 fF.
why: 3D DRAM capacitor blocker: lateral capacitors need half the charge, at the cost of 2x cells, which are cheap in 3D; this may lower the 26-tier break-even.

title: Negative-capacitance bitline element cancels parasitic bitline capacitance
idea: Reverse the sign of the parasitic: a ferroelectric HZO negative-capacitance element at the bitline foot subtracts from the effective bitline capacitance the cell sees, raising the transfer ratio Cs/(Cs+Cbl) from ~0.1 to ~0.3-0.4.
why: Facts 1 and 7: a 3x larger sense signal lets Cs drop to ~2 fF (AR ~25:1) or bitlines grow 3x longer (SA count /3). Hysteresis-free transient NC is the risk.

title: Tungsten-free wordlines driven from both ends with mid-line repeaters
idea: Worse: keep buried wordlines dependent on tungsten, ~80% sourced from China. Flip: switch to supply-safe TiN or doped-poly fill and offset its higher resistance by splitting each local wordline into halves driven from both ends plus a mid-array boost repeater in the sub-wordline driver strip.
why: Scarce-resource intensity (tungsten chokepoint) while holding wordline RC within ~10% of today.

title: Liquid-nitrogen DRAM with double-length copper bitlines
idea: Substitute room-temperature operation with 77 K operation: copper resistivity falls ~7x and junction/GIDL leakage effectively disappears, so bitlines can run 1024 cells instead of 512 and refresh is dropped for datacenter racks with LN2 loops.
why: Periphery area and refresh (facts 3, 7): halving the SA count saves ~15% of die, and refresh energy and bandwidth loss go to ~0.

title: Molybdenum replaces tungsten in wordline straps and contacts
idea: Substitute tungsten wordline straps and periphery contacts with barrier-thin ALD or sputtered molybdenum, which keeps lower resistivity at narrow widths, so each local wordline driver can serve ~2x more cells.
why: Scarce resources and periphery: removes dependence on China-dominated tungsten (~80%) in favor of US-mined Mo, and halves local wordline driver count.

title: Column-gated double-gate access: only requested 64 cells ever open
idea: Limit: never disturb a cell you did not ask for. Give each vertical-channel access transistor a back gate tied to a column-enable line running orthogonally to the wordline, so a cell connects only when wordline AND column-enable are high; only the 64-bit target slice charge-shares, and only its 64 sense amps fire and restore.
why: Destructive read and overfetch (fact 8): ~5.9 pJ per useful bit could fall to ~0.3-0.5 pJ, sense energy -95%, and partial activations reduce row-hammer exposure (fact 9).

title: Bipolar transistor sense amplifiers escape MOS mismatch and BTI
idea: BJT offset depends on emitter-area matching (sigma dVbe ~0.2-0.5 mV) rather than random channel dopants (MOS sigma Vt ~5-15 mV), and BJTs have no gate oxide to suffer BTI drift. Use vertical SiGe BJT latches in a BiCMOS periphery for sensing.
why: ~10x lower offset means ~5-10x less cell charge needed (fact 1); offset stays stable through 10 y at 125 C.

title: Suspension bridge: mid-span regenerator towers double bitline length
idea: A suspension bridge spans far with a few towers. Insert a stripped-down 4-transistor single-ended regenerator (no column switch, equalizer or I/O, compared against a shared mid-rail reference) at the midpoint of each bitline, so bitlines can be 2x longer while the full SA sits only at the end.
why: Periphery area: halving the number of full SA strips (~20% of die) while towers cost ~1/3 of an SA saves ~6-8% die area.

title: Eliminate column decoders and CSL wiring: sense latches as shift registers
idea: After sensing, chain the SA latches into a two-phase shift register (2 transfer gates per SA), so the row buffer clocks out serially to 64 edge taps. The column decoder, the column-select lines and one metal/via level disappear, and the remaining wiring is Cl-etched Al/Mo.
why: Removes the column decoder and CSL (~3-5% of die) and one BEOL level; whole-row streaming suits AI weights, while random-word latency rises.

title: DIMM PMIC takes over VPP and VBB generation
idea: Extend the existing 180/130 nm BCD power-management chip on DDR5 modules with two more rails (VPP ~3 V and a negative VBB) delivered through dedicated balls, so DRAM dies delete their charge pumps and pump decap; inductor-based BCD converters run at ~90% versus ~30-40% for on-die pumps.
why: Periphery area (~5% of die) and energy (fact 10); trailing BCD capacity is plentiful.

title: 8K-TV display fabs build slow periphery as IGZO TFTs on glass
idea: With no EUV available, move every non-speed-critical periphery block (fuse banks, repair maps, test logic, refresh counters, power switches) onto an IGZO TFT glass interposer made in depreciated Gen-8.5 display fabs at 1.5-3 um i-line litho, as 8K panels already drive 2 m lines. The silicon die keeps only cells, SAs and fast decoders.
why: Silicon die area -10-15% and capital per m2 ~50-100x lower for those functions; reuses display capacity instead of EUV tools (fact 4).

title: Stepwise adiabatic restore returns bitline charge to tank rails
idea: Reverse the charge flow on discharge: bitlines are charged and discharged in four steps through intermediate tank-capacitor rails, so charge falling from VDD returns to the tanks instead of ground and restore draws only the top step from the supply; dummy array edges serve as tanks.
why: Fact 10 (CV^2 floor): bitline and restore energy -50-70% with 4 steps, without lowering VARY.

title: Micro-transfer-printed periphery dielets onto array-only wafers
idea: Worse: build every decoder, pump and I/O block in the same costly, EUV-heavy DRAM process. Flip: fabricate pre-tested periphery dielets on cheap logic wafers, release them, and elastomer-stamp transfer-print thousands per pass onto array-only DRAM wafers, then print or plate the short interconnects.
why: Periphery ~49% (fact 7) and capital: DRAM wafer area goes ~90% to cells and only known-good periphery is placed, raising bits per wafer ~1.6x.

title: Twin decaying reference cells written alongside every row
idea: Downhole tools at 200 C see retention collapse to milliseconds; each row carries two reference cells written '1' and '0' at the same instant as its data, and at read they are charge-shared into a mid-level reference that sags exactly as the row's own '1' cells leak. Sensing becomes relative instead of absolute.
why: Refresh interval 2-4x longer at any temperature (fact 3: 16-33% of idle power, 10-20% of bandwidth) for ~0.2% array overhead.

title: CRISPR spacer library of row-hammer attack signatures
idea: Bacteria keep snippets of past viral DNA as spacers to recognize reinfection. The controller keeps a compact CAM of hashed aggressor-pattern signatures (address deltas, cadence relative to refresh), shared fleet-wide by firmware update, and triggers targeted refresh only on matches, over a cheap probabilistic baseline. Firmware, FPGA and attack corpus, ~$500k in 18 months.
why: Fact 9: learns new many-sided patterns after first sighting while issuing ~5x fewer mitigation refreshes than blanket probabilistic schemes.

title: Cool instead of shrink: 77 K lets DUV periphery match EUV
idea: Cryogenic computing users show mobility rises ~2x and leakage vanishes at 77 K; a DRAM whose periphery is built on a DUV-only 28 nm-class process and runs in LN2 pods matches the speed and standby power of an EUV-node room-temperature die.
why: Removes the need for 5-7 EUV layers (fact 4) in periphery and controller, with refresh near zero; trades capex for cryo opex.

title: Po: gain from a negative capacitor — ZrO2 NC input pair
idea: Po: a transistor whose gate amplifies before its channel does. Insert a stabilized ferroelectric ZrO2 layer (Zr is abundant; no Hf) in series with the SA input-pair gate oxide, capacitance-matched so negative capacitance gives ~2x internal voltage gain and sub-60 mV/decade turn-on.
why: Capacitor wall (#1) and voltage floor (#10): ~2x SA input gm per area, so ~30% less signal or a lower SA supply, without hafnium.

title: Tungsten-free periphery contacts using ALD molybdenum and ruthenium
idea: MINIFY tungsten to zero in SA and decoder contacts and local interconnect by depositing Mo or Ru at <=400 C by ALD/CVD, which also lowers contact resistance at small dimensions.
why: Scarce resource (China ~80% of tungsten): removes a chokepoint from periphery; lower resistance speeds narrow periphery wiring.

title: Dendritic-spine IGZO gain stage every 32 cells on short bitlines
idea: Dendritic spines amplify input in a tiny isolated compartment. A BEOL oxide-semiconductor 'spine' transistor every 32 cells takes the cell's charge from a very short local bitline (~1/16 the capacitance) and drives current onto the global bitline. A separate transfer gate writes back.
why: Fact 1/2: the Cs/Cbl transfer ratio improves ~10x, so Cs can fall from ~5 fF to ~1 fF with AR ~15:1 capacitors. That breaks the capacitor wall and makes 3D tiers practical.

title: N: liquid-nitrogen memory pods revive dies rejected for margin
idea: Sell 77 K immersion-cooled memory pods for data centers populated with DRAM dies that failed hot sense-margin or retention bins; at 77 K, MOS mismatch and leakage collapse, so these rejects run at full speed with almost no refresh.
why: Turns 5-15% scrap into product (more usable supply), cuts refresh power (fact 3) to near zero and widens SA margin; nitrogen is abundant, unlike helium.

title: Access-is-refresh mapping puts hot pages on weak rows
idea: Every activation restores a row. The controller maps the most frequently accessed pages onto rows binned as weakest-retention at a 125 C test, so natural traffic refreshes them, while strong rows hold cold data with long refresh.
why: Refresh energy/bandwidth (fact 3) at hot cut ~30-60% with no hardware cost beyond a retention bin table.

title: Communal-kitchen row pre-decoders shared across banks
idea: A Soviet communal apartment shares one kitchen because residents cook at different times. JEDEC's tRRD and tFAW guarantee activates arrive several ns apart, so one fast global row pre-decoder, latched into each bank's local decoder on its ACT, replaces the per-bank pre-decoders.
why: Removes ~75% of row pre-decode logic and its wiring (fact 7), invisible to the controller.

title: Second-life re-binning retunes sensing on retired server DIMMs
idea: Ideal result: no DIMM ever goes to the shredder. A depot tester sweeps each retired module's per-bank tRCD, tWR and refresh margins, writes a custom timing and refresh profile into its SPD, and resells it into edge, client and cache tiers.
why: Usable supply: extends module life 3-5 years, adding supply during a 4x price spike at near-zero capital.

title: H: deuterium-steam gate oxides quiet sense-amp telegraph noise
idea: Grow SA and decoder gate oxides in D2O steam and anneal in D2 so interface traps are capped by deuterium, which resists hot-carrier depassivation, lowering random telegraph noise and Vt drift that force SA oversizing; no rare gases are used.
why: Enables ~30% smaller SA transistors (fact 7) and steadier margin over life.

title: Printed passive equalizer networks replace on-die CTLE and FFE
idea: Worse: keep growing active equalizers and DFE taps inside every DRAM I/O. Flip: print resistor-capacitor-inductor equalization networks (gravure-printed thin-film R and C, printed spiral L) on the package or module flex at each lane to pre-shape the channel passively.
why: Periphery area and I/O power: removes ~10-20% of PHY power and area.

title: Zero-extra-mask lateral bipolar sense amps from BiCMOS DRAM's ashes
idea: Failure mined: Hitachi's 1990s BiCMOS DRAM had superb bipolar sensing but died on extra masks and cost. Fix: form lateral npn transistors in the SA stripe from the existing buried-wordline trench, LDD and contact implants, with no new masks. The bipolar input pairs match Vbe to ~0.5 mV, ~10x better than MOS (5-10 mV).
why: The required bitline signal drops ~5x, so the storage capacitor can shrink ~3-5x (aspect ratio from 70:1 toward 20:1, fact 1) or bitlines can be ~3x longer with fewer SAs.

title: SiGe HBT preamps exploit bipolar matching for tiny signals
idea: MAGNIFY matching precision by switching device physics: one SiGe heterojunction-bipolar differential preamp per 16 bitlines (Vbe mismatch ~1 mV versus 10-20 mV for minimum MOS) amplifies the signal before a CMOS latch.
why: Facts 1 and 10: resolves ~10 mV in ~1 ns, allowing ~3x smaller Cs or VARY ~0.6 V; BiCMOS DRAM died on cost, but periphery on a separate bonded wafer removes that penalty.

title: Telephone-exchange relay logic rebuilt with NEMS relays on glass
idea: Borrowed from relay telephone exchanges, rebuilt with nano-electromechanical relays (metal beam, air gap) made on glass: decoder trees and mat power gates use relays with zero off-current, switched one cycle ahead because addresses arrive early.
why: Idle power: periphery standby leakage goes to ~0, and a relay process needs only metals and oxides, no silicon wafer.

title: Sn: reflowable tin micro-links make field-reprogrammable repair fuses
idea: Replace one-time laser/e-fuses with Sn micro-links in sealed cavities: a Joule pulse melts a link so surface tension beads it open, and a second heater over wetting pads reflows it closed, so repair maps can be rewritten in the field as cells weaken.
why: Enables in-field repair of retention-weak rows (fact 3) and higher usable bits per wafer (~2-5%); reflow links pitch tighter than laser fuses.

title: Inductive charge sloshing reads and restores bits adiabatically
idea: Ideal result: the cell's charge travels to the sense node and returns with zero loss. A shared BEOL spiral inductor between a cell group and the sense node makes the transfer resonant: full charge moves in half an LC period (instead of lossy charge sharing), is sampled at the peak, and swings back to the cell on the next half-period.
why: Facts 1, 8, 10: removes the charge-sharing loss and most restore energy; signal approaches full Cs voltage instead of ~10% transfer ratio, 2-4x lower read energy.

title: Mini-LVDS timing-controller links for on-panel data lines
idea: Borrowed from the reduced-swing differential links between TV timing controllers and source drivers: global data lines on a memory panel become current-mode differential pairs with ~200 mV swing, terminated at each mat cluster.
why: Energy per bit on long panel wires: ~5x lower than full-swing CMOS lines and tolerant of thin-film variation.

title: Limbo bar: back-gate pulse lowers wordline voltage to 1.2 V
idea: Lower the bar instead of jumping higher: give each mat's vertical access transistors a shared back gate held negative in retention (high Vt, low leakage) and pulsed positive only for the accessed mat during activation, so the front wordline needs ~1.2 V instead of ~3 V and can run straight from VDD without charge pumps.
why: Wordline energy falls ~(3/1.2)2 = 6x and pump inefficiency (~3x) disappears, ~15x on the wordline component and the voltage floor (fact 10); back-gate RC sets the activation latency.

title: Lazy restore after power-up: rows restored on first touch
idea: Constraint: data survives power loss via a backup layer, but boot restore must not take milliseconds. A per-row 'restored' bitmap in the periphery, cleared at power-up, lets the memory accept requests immediately; the first touch of a row triggers its restore from the backup layer through the SAs, while a background walker finishes the rest.
why: Instant availability (us instead of ms to s of restore), so NV-backed DRAM suits fast-failover servers and edge devices.

title: Frequency-addressed wordlines replace row decoders with tuned resonators
idea: Ideal result: no decoder at all; the address is broadcast and the right row answers. Each sub-wordline driver gets a tiny BEOL LC or bulk-acoustic resonator tuned to one of 64 frequencies; a global line carries a tone burst and only the matching resonator's rectifier fires its driver, with a 2-level predecode covering 64x64 rows.
why: Periphery area (fact 7): a decoder tree becomes one broadcast line plus passive filters stacked above the drivers; ~30% smaller row-decoder stripe.

title: Skipper-CCD multi-pass sensing reads sub-femtofarad cells
idea: Revive 1970s CCD memory together with the skipper output amplifier. After the access gate opens, the cell's charge packet is clocked back and forth between two transfer gates under a floating-gate electrometer and read non-destructively 16-64 times, then averaged. Noise falls by sqrt(N), so a 1 fF storage node (~6,000 electrons at 1 V) still resolves cleanly.
why: Attacks the capacitor charge wall (fact 1) and destructive read (fact 8). Cs can drop ~4-5x, so pillar aspect ratio can fall from 60-75:1 toward ~20:1. Multi-pass reads add latency, so this suits capacity tiers.

title: Sense-amp resolution time becomes soft information for row LDPC
idea: MINIFY sense margin almost to zero and MAGNIFY the code: each SA's latch-resolution time (slow = low confidence) is captured as a soft bit, and an 8 Kb row-level LDPC codeword (~3% parity) is decoded in the periphery, tolerating raw BER up to 1e-4.
why: Facts 1 and 10: permits VARY ~0.65 V (CV2 array energy -55%) and ~30% smaller Cs; soft information roughly halves parity versus hard-decision codes.

title: Po: only one transistor species — array-device periphery
idea: Po: a DRAM with only one kind of transistor. Build sense amps, sub-wordline drivers and local logic from the same buried-channel/vertical access transistor used in the array (plus a wider-footprint variant), deleting the separate HKMG periphery module.
why: Capital (#4): removes ~10-15 masks and the high-k/metal-gate module, ~8-12% wafer cost and less hafnium; slower periphery is offset with more parallel banks.

title: Open array-to-periphery bond standard for merchant cell wafers
idea: Inverting 'one company makes the whole DRAM die': publish an open hybrid-bond interface (bitline pitch, preamp spec, power and test pads) so array fabs sell bare cell wafers and many periphery designers, including US logic foundries, sell sense/decode dies, like UCIe for memory internals.
why: Splits the $15B integrated fab into an array-only fab plus commodity logic, lowering capital intensity and entry barriers; the US can take periphery share immediately.

title: Wired-NOR zero-detect lines suppress all-zero bursts at sense stripes
idea: Satellites downlink only non-trivial data: each SA group pulls down a wired-NOR line if any latched bit is 1, so all-zero 64-byte sectors return a 1-bit flag instead of a full burst over global I/O and pins. Sparse AI activations and zero-padded KV pages benefit most.
why: I/O energy (fact 5) down 20-50% on sparse data with trivial DUV circuitry.

title: Thin-film-solar steel foil acts as global plate and ground
idea: Borrowed from roll-to-roll CIGS solar on stainless-steel foil: oxide-TFT memory is built on insulated steel foil, and the foil itself, reached through periodic contacts, serves as cell plate, ground return and heat spreader.
why: Periphery: removes plate-line distribution and one or two power-mesh metal layers, and roll-to-roll processing cuts capital per m2.

title: AlN piezoelectric transformer replaces VPP charge pumps
idea: AlN is piezoelectric but not ferroelectric, so it cannot depolarize and works to >500 C. A thin-film AlN resonant piezo transformer steps 1.1 V up to 3 V at high efficiency, replacing multi-stage capacitive VPP/VBB charge pumps.
why: Periphery area and energy (facts 7, 10): pump area ~3-5% of die removed, conversion loss roughly halved.

title: Tungsten-free periphery metal designed for selective recovery
idea: Ideal result: periphery made only of materials you can get back. Replace W contacts and wordline straps with Mo and Ru using liner chemistries chosen for selective wet dissolution, so end-of-life dies yield separable Cu, Mo and Ru streams.
why: Tungsten chokepoint (China ~80%) and recyclability by design.

title: Bit-significance mats: AI weight LSBs on cheap unprotected mats
idea: Box: mixed caps x Si access x two SA grades x bit-plane-split mats x bulk Si x standard. Model weights are stored bit-plane-sliced: MSB planes go to mats with full ECC, while LSB planes go to long-bitline, small-SA, rarely refreshed mats where 1% flips move a value by <0.4% of range, which inference ignores.
why: Unequal error protection: ~60% of bits live on mats with ~40% less periphery and ~10x less refresh.

title: Pooled PCR group testing finds weak-retention cells in field
idea: Borrowed from Dorfman pooled testing: after an extended retention pause, the periphery merges many rows' compare results onto a wired-OR fail bus, flags pools with any failure, and bisects only failing pools; the results fill a per-row refresh-bin table.
why: Refresh (fact 3): cheap in-field profiling enables multi-rate refresh, cutting refresh energy ~50-70% for ~0.1% area.

title: Sacrificial printed fan-out exposes internal test nodes, then dissolves
idea: Worse: dedicate die area to hundreds of large probe pads and on-die test muxes. Flip: inkjet-print a temporary solvent-soluble polymer-and-silver fan-out over the wafer that connects tiny internal test points to large probe pads, test through it, then strip it before final passivation and bumping.
why: Periphery area (fact 7): probe-pad and test-mux area (~2-4% of die) shrinks, with deeper analog visibility into sense amps during test.

title: Downhole-grade FD-SOI periphery wafer bonded under array via bitline mux
idea: Without EUV, put SAs and decoders on a 22-65 nm DUV FD-SOI wafer (the substrate downhole and space chips use for heat and radiation) and hybrid-bond it to an array wafer that holds only cells plus an 8:1 bitline select mux, matching ~0.5 um bond pitch to 30-40 nm bitlines. FD-SOI back-bias trims SA offset per mat.
why: Array die gets ~2x bits per mm2 (fact 7) and periphery moves to a cheap DUV node, removing EUV layers from periphery entirely.

title: Magnify signal ratio with a local gain transistor every 16 cells
idea: Hierarchical bitline: a 16-cell local bitline (~2-3 fF) drives the gate of one local amplifier transistor that conditionally discharges the long global bitline, MAGNIFYING the effective Cs/Cbl ratio from ~1:10 to ~1:1.
why: Facts 1-2: a 1-1.5 fF capacitor becomes readable, removing the AR wall and making short capacitors in 3D tiers viable; ~6-8% area spent on local amps.

title: Pacinian-corpuscle auto-zero sense amp responding only to change
idea: Pacinian corpuscles ignore steady pressure and respond only to change. Before the wordline fires, each sense amp stores its own input offset on small capacitors while the bitlines are equalized (auto-zero). It then senses only the change, cancelling latch Vt mismatch.
why: Fact 1/7: input devices are oversized to hold offset below ~10 mV. Offset cancellation lets them shrink ~4x, cutting sense-amp stripe area ~30% or Cs ~30%.

title: MKID frequency multiplexing reads hundreds of segments per line
idea: Borrowed from astronomy's microwave kinetic inductance detector readout: on low-loss fused silica, each bitline segment gets a thin-film LC resonator at its own frequency whose Q is loaded by the selected cell's state, and one feedline carrying a frequency comb reads ~100-500 segments at once.
why: Periphery: one wideband receiver per feedline replaces hundreds of sense amps and column muxes; glass's low loss tangent makes inductors practical where silicon substrates kill Q.

title: FD-SOI periphery with PTAT back-bias flattens hot leakage
idea: Build periphery on fully-depleted SOI: buried oxide removes most junction area (generation leakage scales with ni and junction area), and a PTAT back-bias generator raises Vt ~1 mV/K as temperature climbs, holding standby leakage roughly flat from 25 to 125 C.
why: Periphery standby power at hot down ~5-10x; less self-heating feedback on retention.

title: Thin-film Schottky diode-matrix passive row decoder
idea: Substitute transistor NAND decode trees with a 1950s-style diode-matrix decoder made of thin-film Pt/IGZO Schottky diodes at address-line crossings, so only the selected row line stays high. It needs two masks plus sputtering.
why: Periphery area: decode moves into a passive crossbar layer that can sit over the array, and the transistor count of decoders drops ~5x.

title: Flying-shuttle sense enable rides the wordline's RC wave
idea: Like Kay's flying shuttle carrying the weft across every warp in one throw, route sense-enable on a delay-matched line parallel to the wordline. Each SA then fires just after its own cell's wordline actually rises, instead of every SA waiting for the slowest far-end cell.
why: Removes worst-case wordline-RC margin from tRCD (~2-4 ns of ~14 ns, ~20% faster activate) and allows 2x longer wordlines, so half as many sub-wordline driver strips (~5% die).

title: Token-synchronous memory: decode sweeps restore every row each token
idea: Align the workload clock with the leakage clock: LLM decode reads all dense weights and active KV each token (~20-50 ms) and every DRAM read restores its row, so the refresh engine is removed from the die; a 1-bit-per-row coverage bitmap faults if any row goes unread for one retention window, and sparse MoE experts live in an NV tier.
why: Zero refresh power and 10-20% of bandwidth returned (fact 3); refresh counters and logic leave the periphery (fact 7).

title: HBM buyback harvests base dies and good DRAM layers
idea: Ideal result: every die returns to service. Vendors pay a deposit-refund on HBM-equipped modules; returned stacks with reversible bonds are disassembled, dies retested, and good DRAM layers restacked onto new base dies.
why: Supply and capital: recovers bits at a fraction of new-wafer cost and offsets HBM's ~3x wafer area per bit (fact 6).

title: Sense amps built from the array's own vertical transistors
idea: Reverse the borrowing: instead of the array borrowing logic transistors, SAs and sub-wordline drivers are built from the same vertical-channel 4F2 pillars as the access transistors, in the same steps and pitch-matched under the bitlines, so one U.S. memory fab runs the full flow with no logic module or partner.
why: Facts 4 and 7: ~8-12 fewer masks, SA strip area ~-30%, whole die in one U.S. fab.

title: Po: the chip forgets its repairs — off-die repair maps
idea: Po: a chip that does not remember where it is broken. Delete on-die e-fuse/antifuse banks and their HV programming; store row/column repair maps in module SPD flash or the controller, upload them at boot over a sideband into a small CAM per bank, and update them in the field as weak rows appear.
why: Periphery (#7) and usable supply: frees ~2-4% of die, removes silicide fuse links, and field-updatable repair raises effective yield and lifetime.

title: Spare cell-capacitor pillars serve as charge-pump flying capacitors
idea: Substitute planar MOS capacitors in the VPP/VBB charge pumps with blocks of ordinary high-aspect-ratio array capacitor pillars, placed in dummy mats and wired in parallel as flying and reservoir capacitors.
why: Periphery area: array caps store ~50-100x more charge per um^2 than gate-oxide caps, shrinking pump area ~80% (pumps are several % of die) with zero new process steps.

title: Negative-capacitance film cancels bitline parasitic capacitance
idea: Box: pillar cap x Si access x NC-compensated bitline x in-line HZO capacitor x Si x ALD ferroelectric. A stabilized negative-capacitance HZO element on the bitline subtracts most of its parasitic capacitance during charge sharing, raising the transfer ratio Cs/(Cs+Cbl) from ~0.1 toward ~0.4.
why: 3-4x more signal from the same 5 fF cell, so Cs can shrink (AR 60:1 toward 20:1) or bitlines can lengthen; attacks the capacitor wall.

title: Superregenerative quench latch converts bitline signal into time
idea: Borrow Armstrong's 1922 superregenerative receiver. The sense latch is biased just past instability and quenched every cycle, so the tiny bitline differential grows exponentially and its time-to-threshold is proportional to ln(signal). A 6-bit time-to-digital counter at the mat edge decodes 2-bit-per-cell levels from one latch, with no ADC ladder.
why: Enables multi-level DRAM (2 bits/cell) at existing sense-amp pitch: ~2x bits per capacitor and half the sense amps per bit (fact 7 periphery share, fact 1 charge wall).

title: Local quality: few precision sense amps steered to weak columns
idea: TRIZ #3 Local quality replaces uniform sense amps: 7 of every 8 are minimum-size latches and 1 of 8 is a large offset-cancelled precision amp. Wafer test maps columns with weak cells or high-offset latches, and a column steering mux routes only those bitlines to the precision amps.
why: Facts 1 and 7: the worst-case tail sets device size for only ~12% of amps, so sense-amp strip area falls ~35% while read margin is kept for the ~1% weak-cell tail.

title: Henneman size-principle recruitment of charge-pump units
idea: Muscles recruit small motor units first and large ones only under heavy load (Henneman's size principle). Each VPP/VBB pump is split into binary-weighted units (1x, 2x, 4x, 8x) enabled in order by a load monitor, so light loads run on small units at peak efficiency. Validated on a 65/130 nm MPW test chip and licensed, ~$700k in 24 months.
why: Fact 10/idle power: pumps are 20-40% efficient at light load. Recruitment roughly doubles that, cutting VPP/VBB standby and refresh power ~30-50%.

title: Resonant clock grid with electroplated copper inductors
idea: Thick electroplated Cu spiral inductors (<=250 C) in top metal resonate with the periphery clock-grid capacitance, recycling clock energy each cycle instead of dumping it, MINIFYING clock and DLL power.
why: Fact 5: clock power -40%, worth ~5-8% of DRAM interface power; uses only mature low-temperature steps.

title: Po: the charge pump is a magnet — NiFe inductor boost
idea: Po: a charge pump replaced by a magnet. Generate VPP with an on-die inductive boost converter using thin-film permalloy (NiFe)-cored spiral inductors in the top Al/Cu level, switched at ~100 MHz by thick-oxide silicon devices.
why: Voltage floor (#10) and periphery (#7): ~75-85% efficient vs ~30-40% for charge pumps, halving VPP energy and freeing pump capacitor area; Ni and Fe are abundant.
